data.text:
Napalm, one of the most devastating incendiary weapons ever created, was born not on a battlefield but in the basement of a Harvard University chemistry laboratory on Valentine's Day, 1942.

The man behind its creation was Louis Fieser, a respected organic chemist and beloved professor who had spent his career studying blood-clotting agents, antimalarial drugs, and steroids before the war redirected his talents toward destruction.

Prior to his work on napalm, Fieser had been tasked with developing poisonous gases, a project he personally disliked but accepted out of duty before his focus shifted toward incendiaries.

The immediate catalyst for napalm's development was a rubber shortage. When the Japanese army captured rubber plantations across Malaya, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Thailand, natural latex — essential for early incendiary devices — became nearly impossible to obtain.

On February 14, 1942, Fieser and his team reported to the National Defense Research Council that a powder made with aluminum naphthenate and aluminum palmitate could be stirred with gasoline at room temperature to produce strong, tough, and flammable gels.

The name napalm itself was a portmanteau drawn from two of its core chemical components: naphthenic acid and palmitic acid.

The six-man group worked in total secrecy for four years, with Fieser giving up his regular teaching duties while Harvard contributed his salary to the war effort off the record; the National Defense Research Council contract for just the incendiary project totaled $359,125.

Fieser even kept the project secret from his own wife, who only learned of it weeks later when she met a military officer at the airport who casually asked how her husband's incendiary project was progressing.

The first public demonstration came on July 4, 1942, when Fieser detonated a live napalm bomb on the Harvard College soccer field, flooding a circular pool and igniting a spectacular 2,100-degree Fahrenheit fire cloud that sent flaming lumps of gel splashing through the water while nearby tennis players watched in stunned disbelief.

Fieser mastered the correct combination of gasoline and chemicals to ensure the incendiary cocktail could completely wipe out buildings and infrastructure, finding it to be six times stronger than thermite and capable of continuing to burn until it consumed whatever surface it had adhered to.

One of Fieser's colleagues also suggested adding phosphorus to the mixture, which increased its ability to penetrate deeply into dense material, where it would continue to burn long after initial ignition.

The weapon was approved for front-line use in 1943, and its combat debut came in Sicily, where American troops with napalm-fueled flamethrowers burned a wheat field believed to be sheltering German forces.

Two-thirds of all napalm bombs produced during World War II were used in the Pacific, deployed against deeply entrenched Japanese fortifications on Saipan, Iwo Jima, the Philippines, and Okinawa.

General Curtis LeMay, facing a shortage of conventional thermite bombs, ordered air raids on Japan to shift to napalm, and a 1946 report claimed that 40,000 tons of M69 incendiary bombs were dropped on Japan throughout the war, damaging 64 cities and causing more deaths than the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki combined.

Napalm also saw use in the European theater, targeting German fortifications and transportation hubs during Operation Overlord and the Battle of the Bulge, though its reach sometimes had tragic unintended consequences, as when it inadvertently killed French civilians near the town of Royan.

During the Korean War, napalm became the air war's signature weapon. On an average good day, United Nations pilots used 260,000 liters of napalm, with American forces accounting for the vast majority of that total.

📍 Route Highlights: 
Seetarambagh ➔ Bhoiguda Kaman ➔ Mangalhat ➔ Puranapul ➔ Jumerath Bazar ➔ Begum Bazar ➔ MJ Market ➔ Koti ➔ Sultan Bazar.

🚧 Key Diversion Points:
🔹 Traffic from Asif Nagar diverted at Mallepally X Roads.
🔹 Traffic from Puranapool diverted towards Karwan/100 Feet Road.
🔹 Traffic from MJ Bridge/Abids diverted towards alternate routes at MJ Market & GPO.
🔹 Traffic from Chaderghat/Narayanaguda diverted at Rangmahal & Kachiguda X Roads.
*(Note: Diversions will be lifted progressively as the procession passes each junction).*

⚠️ Expect Heavy Congestion at: 
Begum Bazar Chatri, Afzalgunj, MJ Market, Abids GPO, Putlibowli X Roads, Koti Andhra Bank, Chaderghat, and Kachiguda.

Commuters are requested to plan their journeys accordingly and use alternate routes to avoid delays. Your cooperation with the Hyderabad Traffic Police is highly appreciated. 🤝

The five-second epistemology of the deli counter ticket arriving at the White House.

The IRGC said $200 on Day 1. The kitchen said $200 on Day 3. Goldman said $65 on Day 3. Then $77. Then $85. Then $93. Then $110 in the extreme scenario. Twenty-seven days of revisions chasing the number Iran published on the first morning. And now the White House is examining $200. Examining. The architecture examining the number the IRGC handed them on a ticket twenty-seven days ago. The architecture just pulled a number at the deli counter and the number is the number the IRGC has been serving since the counter opened. Welcome to the deli. Your number was called three weeks ago. Ghalibaf da Gangsta has been behind the counter the entire time.

Examining what $200 would mean for the economy. Examining. The way you examine a fire while standing in it. The way you examine the water while drowning. The Philippines already declared a national energy emergency. Slovenia is already rationing. Shell already said Europe faces shortages next month. The breakeven already hit 2.06%. Hapag-Lloyd can’t rescue its own team. The LNG is evaporating off ships. And the architecture is examining. Senior officials studying possible fallout from extreme scenarios. The extreme scenario that the IRGC named on Day 1. The extreme scenario that Dubai physical already hit at $166. The extreme scenario that the kitchen already wrote about while the architecture was still examining $65.

Ghalibaf da Gangsta asked if they can print gas molecules. The architecture is examining whether it can afford the molecules it can’t print. Goldman holds a ticket. Citi holds a ticket. BlackRock holds a ticket. The White House just pulled a ticket. The IRGC is still behind the counter. The ticket is still in Farsi. They still don’t teach Farsi at the White House. Some examination. Some $200. Some deli counter. Some empire. Day 27.
